notes: Walks the checked CEL AST for `ph()` calls with literal names and flags non-literal names as dynamic, so only expressions that actually read response placeholders are evaluated against the response. This covers every behavior the maintainers asked for, including escaped literals, look-alike names and dynamic names. It also adds thorough unit tests and an end-to-end POST regression test; the only small nit is that `Placeholders()` returns the internal slice without copying it.

Walks the checked CEL AST to find placeholder names, treating names that are not string literals as dynamic, then retries on responses only for the status, status_text, latency and header.* placeholders, so it matches the reference semantics. Its tests cover every case the maintainers listed (upstream.host, escaped literal, status_codes, direct ph() call, dynamic name) plus an end-to-end POST that is not retried. Minor nit: Placeholders() returns the internal slice instead of a copy.

Fixes both root causes: a caller with a direct child still `cancelling` is re-aggregated instead of written `cancelled`, which works at any nesting depth because cancellation runs deepest-first, and `cancelRun` now emits when no job changed but the run is done. It differs slightly from the reference: it always returns the reloaded caller even if its status is unchanged, and it re-emits for runs that were already done, both harmless; it also adds solid nested-caller and concurrency-waiter tests.

Fixes both bugs: a caller now stays cancelling while any direct child is cancelling (re-aggregated through RefreshReusableCallerStatus inside cancelOneJob, which works for nested callers because descendants are processed deepest-first), and the concurrency emitter now runs after a cancel that updated no jobs; differences from the reference are an extra child query per caller cancel, returning the reloaded caller even when its status is unchanged, and an emit condition (`IsDone`) that is broader than the reference's status-changed check, though harmless, with strong tests covering nested callers through runner ack and force-cancel waking the blocked run.

The core fix matches the reference: `Close` is added to the interface, `Get`/`Walk` reconnect a closed connection, `Reconnect` resets the USM engine ID/boots/time, and `Gather` closes the connection on field or table failure. Clearing the localized keys is redundant, since gosnmp already regenerates them when the engine ID changes, but harmless. The added tests on the wrapper and on `Gather` are solid. Scope is hurt by an unrelated edit to `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (path handling and an added `Log`), which looks like a local-environment workaround. The package suite also failed; the cause is not established and may be environmental.

The core fix matches the reference: `Close()` is added to the interface, closed connections are reconnected before `Get`/`Walk`, the USM engine ID, boots and time are reset on reconnect, and the agent's connection is closed after field or table errors. Clearing `SecretKey`/`PrivacyKey` is redundant because gosnmp already regenerates them when the engine ID changes, but it does no harm. The new wrapper- and plugin-level tests are solid, but the patch also rewrites the unrelated `TestSnmpInitGosmi` (path and logger) as an environment workaround, and the package suite failed.

Core --links support works for both zip and squashfs: symlinks are skipped with a notice naming the flag, listed with the .rclonelink suffix, and reads honour range and seek. But it adds a heavier extra layer: a case-insensitive LinkFilter that silently drops clashing entries, including regular *.rclonelink members (contrary to the 'stays a regular file' requirement); eager opening of every zip symlink at listing time; a 4KiB target cap; and an O(n) Info() scan in squashfs NewObject. These choices diverge from the reference and likely explain the failed hidden test, despite thorough tests of its own.

Adds --links support to both backends with suffix naming, a length-based size, range/seek-aware Open, and List/NewObject agreement. It also adds an extra LinkFilter that drops symlinks, and even regular .rclonelink members, when they clash with other entries; this goes beyond the spec, contradicts 'stays a regular file' in clash cases, and likely explains the failed hidden test. The zip side eagerly opens and reads every symlink member during readZip, which is costly for archives on S3, and the squashfs side logs per bad symlink despite the log-flooding concern; tests are thorough and include a real copy-escape check.

Fixes the root cause of the leaked socket and the wrong unlink path, using a refcounted unixSocket record under a separate lock with double-close guards and abstract-socket handling. The reasoning about the reload race holds up. However, it rewrites the internal socket types and map, switches deleteListener/deletePacketConn to pointer receivers, and changes listenerPool counting for reused sockets. That refactor is far broader than the targeted fix, breaks every hidden white-box test (0/7), and fails the package suite, despite its own fairly thorough tests.

The new shared unixSocket object (one kept dup fd, refs and unlink handled under a separate mutex) fixes the leaked File() dup and covers last-holder unlink, double close returning ErrClosed, the close/listen race and abstract names. It also rewrites internal types: unixListener/unixConn lose mapKey/count, reused sockets come back wrapped in *deleteListener, and the delete wrappers switch to pointer receivers. That broader rewrite, plus the unrelated listeners.go change, is the likely reason the package suite fails and 0/7 hidden tests pass, and it treats '@' paths as abstract on every OS, not just Linux.

Fixes the parser well: any single-component prefix is stripped, /dev/null is kept, a path with no prefix resolves to empty, rename/copy-to lines take priority, and the diff --git line is split where both halves name the same path. It forces a/ and b/ with --src-prefix/--dst-prefix CLI args, which reliably override noprefix, srcPrefix, dstPrefix and mnemonicPrefix, but this also hides the user's mnemonic prefixes in the displayed diff and skips stash show; unit and integration tests are thorough.

Generalizes prefix stripping to any single leading component (keeping /dev/null and returning empty for unprefixed paths), adds the rename-to/copy-to fallback, and replaces the b/-based split of the diff --git line with a same-path split, all matching the spec; it forces a/ and b/ through --src-prefix/--dst-prefix command-line flags instead of config, which overrides the user's mnemonic prefixes in displayed diffs (a defensible but less user-friendly choice), and it misses stash show; the unit tests are thorough and come with an integration test.

C1 fixes the bug in all three GC paths (Truncate, selected, stale): it keeps the series identity while an exemplar is at or after the cutoff, releases the chunks and appender, keeps the mmap-ready and chunk metrics correct, and covers WAL replay and snapshot restore. Its tests are broad and pass. Weaknesses: the exemplar timestamp is recorded at commit rather than at append, so an appended-but-uncommitted exemplar on an unreserved series is not protected. It also steals a bit from the pending-commit counter mask and re-implements chunk truncation instead of reusing truncateChunksBefore. Finally, the new head test is inserted between an existing test's doc comment and that test's function, so the comment now sits on the wrong function.

C1 matches the reference across all three compaction paths, the Truncate path, WAL replay and snapshot restore, releases chunks with correct metrics and mmap-ready accounting, and treats zero and negative timestamps correctly; however, it records the exemplar at commit instead of at append, so an AppenderV1 exemplar on a series with no sample in that batch is not protected from GC before commit, it shrinks the pending-commit mask to fit a flag bit, and the new head test is inserted between an existing test's doc comment and its function.
